jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

Socket helps devs and security teams ship faster by cutting out security busywork. Thousands of orgs use Socket to safely find, audit, and manage open source code. Our customers - from Anthropic to xAI, and Figma to Vercel - love Socket (just check out their tweets https://socket.dev/love to see for yourself!)


Founded by Feross Aboukhadijeh https://www.linkedin.com/in/feross/, a long-time open source maintainer with software downloaded over a billion times a month, Socket has raised $ https://socket.dev/blog/series-b125M in funding https://socket.dev/blog/series-c from top angels, operators, and security leaders.



About the Role

We’re hiring Socket’s first Product Manager. You’ll come in at a point where there’s real product-market pull, a growing customer base, and a lot of room to shape what comes next. You’ll have a direct hand in deciding what we build, why we build it, and where Socket goes from here.



You'll work closely with leadership and engineering to shape Socket's product strategy: understanding where customers are heading, identifying the problems we should solve, deciding where to invest, and turning those decisions into clear priorities and shipped products. You'll spend real time with developers and security teams, work closely with Customer Engineering and Sales, and bring those perspectives back to the team to help shape what we build next.



You'll also build the product practices that will help Socket scale: how we prioritize, make tradeoffs, define success, roadmap, and communicate what we're building and why. You won't be inheriting a playbook. You'll be building it.



What you’ll do:

 - Own prioritization across customer commitments, support escalations, reliability work, and new opportunities, and be clear about what each new commitment displaces.

 - Dig underneath feature requests. Talk directly with customers, sit in on CE and Sales calls, and test proposed solutions early enough to change course.

 - Partner with engineers and designers to turn priorities into requirements, user stories, success criteria, and project plans with owners, dependencies, and milestones.

 - Engage seriously with technical constraints, balancing cost when evaluating options.

 - Keep a current picture of what we've committed to, from contractual obligations to exploratory work, and give GTM orgs clear guidance on what they can promise, what they can discuss, and how firm the timelines are.

 - Write down the expected benefit and key assumptions behind each investment, follow up on adoption and outcomes, and bring what you learn into the next round of decisions.



What you’ll bring:

 - Several years of product management experience, ideally owning developer-facing, security, or infrastructure products in a B2B SaaS environment.

 - A track record of making hard prioritization calls under real capacity limits. You're comfortable saying no, defining product boundaries, and making trade-offs explicit.

 - Technical enough to hold your own with engineers and customers alike, and to move easily between customer conversations, product strategy, detailed requirements, and technical trade offs. You know what a CI/CD pipeline does, what a lockfile is for, and why a check that adds two minutes to every build gets ripped out.

 - Customer curiosity. You get to the underlying problem instead of just passing along feature requests, and you confirm your understanding without making promises we can't keep.

 - You earn trust with engineers by bringing context, asking strong questions, and respecting their technical ownership, and you can influence Engineering, Customer Engineering, Sales, and leadership without relying on formal authority.

 - Strong project management instincts. You surface risks early and keep people aligned when scope or timing changes.

 - Clear, concise written communication. We work heavily async, so being able to write clearly, explain the why behind decisions, and keep everyone aligned matters.

 - Builder mindset. There’s no product playbook yet. You’ll help build it from the ground up.

 - Preferred:
   
   - Experience with software supply chain security, application security, vulnerability management, or security platforms.
   
   - Experience building products for developers or security teams.
   
   - Familiarity with enterprise software evaluation, technical sales cycles, and customer-driven roadmap pressure.
   
   - Experience joining as an early or first dedicated Product Manager.



Hiring is a big decision on both sides. Read more about our Hiring Philosophy  https://socket.dev/hiring-philosophyand how we approach the process at Socket.



Benefits: Our benefits are crafted to support you and your family, so you can take care of what matters most and thrive in and outside of work. We offer:

 - Market competitive salary bands

 - Meaningful equity program

 - Comprehensive health benefits for you and your family (99% coverage)

 - Flexible time-off, holidays, and winter shutdown to rest & recharge

 - Paid parental leave

 - Remote-first, with quarterly team off-sites 



At Socket, we

 1. Pursue Excellence: We set ourselves apart by consistently delivering work of exceptional quality and distinction.

 2. Move with urgency and focus: We prioritize swift, decisive action.

 3. Think rigorously: We care about being right and it often takes reasoning from first principles to get there. We value alternative perspectives and have constructive discussions.

 4. Trust and amplify: We overtrust, always assume good intent, and give specific feedback to help each other improve.

 5. Feel a strong sense of ownership: We wear many hats and feel a strong sense of overall ownership of the company and we're non-territorial regarding our nominal domains.

 6. Are customer obsessed: We relentlessly prioritize the needs of our customers, striving to exceed their expectations and delight them at every interaction.
